clauses.reason: The adoption of the Administrator's report, the finding of no extreme hardship and the denial of the exemption application were performed when the order was signed on August 4, 1933 ('it is hereby, denied'). A one-time determination is exhausted by performance (owner ruling 2026-10-28); the applicants' continued subjection to the Cotton Textile Code is a consequence that comes from the code, not a command of this order. Actor: EO 6242-E itself. Date: the order's date line, 'August 4, 1933'.

The exception preserved the Administrator's July 30, 1933 stay for the applicants 'pending my final determination' of the Rubber Manufacturers' Association application. It ended when the stay ended: EO 6476 (December 4, 1933) denied the application and ordered 'that said stay shall be terminated and the provisions of said code ... shall be in full force and effect from and after December 11, 1933', so the exception ended on 1933-12-11. Actor: EO 6476. Later events: EO 6407 (1933-11-06), which scheduled a termination for 1933-11-13 that was extended (EO 6424 of November 13 to November 20, and EO 6463 of November 27, held APP text read in full and page-checked but not pinned as evidence because its page bytes are only a custody record, extended the termination date until the hearings were completed). Disclosed alternative: 1933-12-04, the date of the determination in EO 6476.

research_rationale:
Identity and text (APP page check, jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, done 2026-10-29): the registered American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved) was read in full. The MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with the same sha256 (0e20ac69f3ff...) has the heading 'Executive Order 6242-E—In the Matter of the Application of Dwight Manufacturing Co. for Certain Exemptions from the Cotton Textile Code', the date 1933-08-04 (which agrees with the date line of the held text), and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's; the row records the common-crawl WARC location. The 1944 WPA numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv) carries the same number and date: 'Application of the Dwight Manufacturing Co. for cer tain exemptions from Code of Fair Competition for the Cotton Textile Industry denied. I NRA Codes 727. (Aug 4, 1933)'. Quotations are taken from the registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. This is not a code approval, so TR-NRA-CODE does not fit (its machine typing is only a lead). EO 6242-E (August 4, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt, on the Administrator's recommendation) adopts the Administrator's report, finds that no case of injustice and extreme hardship requiring special treatment has been made out, and orders that the application for exemption by 'the above-named applicants' (the page heading names Dwight Manufacturing Co.) from the limitation on the use of productive machinery in the Cotton Textile Code 'be, and it is hereby, denied, except as said applicants may be affected by the stay of the code granted by the Administrator's order of July 30, 1933, pending my final determination of the issues raised in the application for exemption filed by the Rubber Manufacturer's Association with reference to the limitation of use of machinery for the production of tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires.' The dossier's single clause (characters 541-1873) joins two components with different lifetimes, so the inventory is corrected on the registered text into the denial (541-1403) and the exception for the stay (1404-1771); the signature and recommendation are not operative. Denial: a one-time determination performed when the order was signed. Under the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling (exhausted by performance, with the surviving consequence separated) it is recorded as exhausted on 1933-08-04, the order's date line; that the applicants stayed subject to the code is a consequence that comes from the code, not a continuing command of this order. Exception: it preserved the Administrator's stay for these applicants. Stay history from the held later orders (APP texts, page-checked): EO 6407 (November 6, 1933) recites that the Administrator on July 30, 1933 'further stayed the application of said provision of the code pending determination by me of the issues raised by the application for exemption', denies the application and orders that 'beginning November 13, 1933, the above-mentioned stay of said provision shall be terminated'. EO 6424 (November 13, 1933; the held APP page for it carries another order's title and is not used, but its text, matching the Commons printed copy at jobs/hathi-gpo-orders/output/texts/EO_6424.txt and the WPA entry 'extended to Nov. 20, 1933', 'modifie[s]' EO 6407 'by extending the termination date of said stay to November 20, 1933') is known to the claim through EO 6463's recital. EO 6463 (November 27, 1933) recites that the orders of November 6 and 13 'terminate on November 20, 1933, the stay now in effect' and 'modifie[s]' them 'by extending the termination date of said stay until the completion of said hearings and determination by me'. EO 6476 (December 4, 1933) recites that the application of the code 'has been stayed pending a determination by me of the issues raised', denies the application, and orders 'that said stay shall be terminated and the provisions of said code with reference to the limitation of the use of productive machinery as applied to the production of tire yarns or fabrics for rubber tires shall be in full force and effect from and after December 11, 1933.' Reading: the exception lasts as long as the stay it preserves, and the stay ended 'from and after December 11, 1933' (its last day was December 10; EO 6476 speaks of the code applying from that day, so no inclusive 'until' reading is involved). The first end of the exception is therefore 1933-12-11, by EO 6476. Disclosed alternatives: (a) the exception's words 'pending my final determination' could end it with the determination, EO 6476's date 1933-12-04, seven days earlier; I read the exception as tracking the stay, which EO 6476 itself kept in force until December 11. (b) EO 6407's scheduled termination (1933-11-13) and the November 20 date were not ends, because each termination date was extended before it took effect (EO 6424, then EO 6463; EO 6407 is recorded as a later event on the clause, while EO 6463 is relied on from the held APP text but not pinned as an evidence reference, because the raw page bytes for its sha256 are held only as a custody record and the checker leaves that source unverified). (c) EO 6463 is dated November 27, after the November 20 termination date it extends and calls the stay 'now in effect'; no held source shows a lapse between November 20 and 27, and EO 6476 treats the stay as continuous, so none is claimed; had the stay lapsed on November 20 the exception would have ended on 1933-11-20. The Administrator's order of July 30, 1933 is known only through the recitals of EO 6407 and EO 6476 and is not held; it is not needed to date the end. Whole-order end: 1933-12-11. The Cotton Textile Code itself is a different instrument and continued. Searches run 2026-10-29. (1) A scan of 51,237 txt, jsonl, csv, json and md files under jobs/ (skipping the derivative folders clause-drafts, claim-kit, case-bundles, claim-drafts, x1-class-engine, readiness-tracker and domesday-register, and cache, capture and pdf folders) for the code's title and for citations of this order by number. (2) Every held order text numbered 7060 or higher (APP, Hathi/Commons printed copies, Wikisource, Federal Register, source-ladder) containing the phrase 'codes of fair competition': only EO 7075, EO 7076 and EO 7323 (and an unrelated 1941 board order, EO 9027). (3) The APP index of orders dated 1935-05-15 through 1935-06-25: no order dated 1935-05-27 through 1935-06-14 touches an NRA code; EO 7075 and 7076 (June 15) and EO 7084 and 7085 (June 24, labor boards) are the next NRA orders. (4) The later-events counter-evidence leads file (none for this order). (5) The machine searches current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr (0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (0 hits; its coverage starts in 1937, so it is not relied on alone). Result of (1) and a further scan of held order texts for 'tire yarns or fabrics': EO 6242-C, 6242-D and 6242-E (sister denials of the same date with the same exception), EO 6407, 6424 (text), 6463 and 6476 (APP), and printed copies of 6407, 6424, 6463 and 6476; no other held text names the exception or this applicant, and no held order after EO 6476 mentions the stay.

savings.reason: The denial leaves the applicants without an exemption; that status follows from the Cotton Textile Code and accrued on 1933-08-04, and does not depend on a continuing command of this order. Production and hours worked under the stay before 1933-12-11 are accrued effects. The order states no savings clause, and EO 6476 states that the code limitation applied in full from and after 1933-12-11.
